inline_comments.comment: The condition `isAlreadyTransformed && !hasNamedExports` is applied identically for both `'main'` and `'preview'` configTypes, but the two types have different semantics elsewhere in the function (e.g., Scenario 4 adds an empty default export only for preview). Per the project coding rule, any modification to a configType-specific branch must explicitly document whether the same logic applies to the other config type. Add a brief comment explaining why the identical condition is correct here for both types — or split it into a per-type condition as done in the broader `shouldSkipTransform` pattern below.

general_comments.comment: No test is added for the specific regression this PR fixes (Windows CRLF introduced by `recast` on already-transformed files). The existing 'should leave already transformed code as is' test uses `.toEqual(original)`, which passes even if a round-trip through `recast` normalises line endings on Unix. Consider adding an assertion that explicitly verifies `result === original` (strict identity or byte count) so a future refactor that re-enables `recast` for this path is caught immediately. Alternatively, the test description should call out the Windows line-ending concern so reviewers know what behaviour it guards.
